title: Gate a VCF Automation storage-class mutation behind a placement precheck derived from reference docs
reference_patch_apply: git apply -p1 --directory=files reference_fix.patch (from the seed root)
deliverable: src/vcfa_storage/client.py implementing StorageProfileClient.get_region, get_datastore and create_vsphere_storage_profile.
prompt:
`vcfa-storage-profile` is the small Python package our platform CI runs to materialise VCF Automation vSphere storage classes from definitions checked into git. It targets VCF Automation in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 -- the successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation.

VCF Automation publishes no machine-readable API specification, so `docs/contract.json` is a hand transcription of the Broadcom xAPIs reference pages recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. Read the contract first. It is the authority for paths, methods, headers, query parameters, body fields and the placement precheck, and it marks which parts are literal transcription and which are inference.

`src/vcfa_storage/client.py` is a stub. Implement its three methods.

`get_region(region_id)` -- call the contract's `getRegion` operation and return the decoded `Region`, or `None` on 404. Raise `ApiError` (from `vcfa_storage.errors`) on any other non-2xx.

`get_datastore(datastore_id)` -- call `getFabricVsphereDatastore` and return the decoded datastore, or `None` on 404. Raise `ApiError` on any other non-2xx.

`create_vsphere_storage_profile(...)` -- create one vSphere storage class and return it as the appliance stored it.

The thing to get right is that `createVsphereStorageProfile` is mutating and the reference documents no 404 for it, so a bad region or a datastore in the wrong datacenter comes back as an opaque 400 -- or worse, as a storage class that provisioning silently cannot place. Run the contract's placement precheck first and completely. If any part of it fails, the mutation must not be sent at all, so nothing on the appliance is changed. Report a refusal with the matching `PrecheckFailed` subclass: `RegionNotFoundError`, `DatastoreNotFoundError` or `PlacementMismatchError`. A mutation that the appliance itself rejects is an `ApiError`, not a precheck refusal.

The request body has to be exact. `name`, `regionId` and `defaultItem` are the three fields the contract marks required and are always present. For every optional argument in the provided signature, `None` is the "not supplied" sentinel and its field must be absent from the JSON object. Every non-`None` value must be present, even when it is `""`, `0`, `false` or `[]`, because the appliance reads an absent field as "leave at the documented default" and a present one as an explicit instruction. In particular, `default_item=False` is required and must still be sent, `priority=0` is the highest priority rather than a missing value, and `supports_encryption=False` is a real instruction. The same rule governs the optional `apiVersion` query parameter: when the client has no `api_version` configured, the parameter must not appear in the query string at all.

Constraints:

- Python 3.9+ standard library only. No third-party packages. The only host the client may contact is the `base_url` it was constructed with.
- Do not edit `tests/`, `docs/contract.json` or `docs/official_sources.json`.
- `bash run_verification.sh` must pass.

verification.notes: Runs tests/test_contract.py (41 unittest cases) against the loopback mock in tests/vcfa_mock.py. The mock binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port, builds its routing table from docs/contract.json so it serves only the three operations the contract names, answers 501 to anything else, and appends every request it receives to a JSONL log the tests read back. That log is how the suite proves a failing precheck sent no mutating request. The mock has no clock and no randomness: minted ids are counter-derived and timestamps are fixed, and every counter rewinds between tests, so runs are identical regardless of order or PYTHONHASHSEED. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. The shipped stub fails; with reference_fix.patch applied the suite reports OK.

contract_provenance.note: VCF Automation is absent from the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository (Apache-2.0) and the Broadcom Developer Portal serves no downloadable OpenAPI document for this API set. docs/contract.json was transcribed by hand on 2026-08-11 from the developer.broadcom.com xAPIs reference pages and says so in its own source_statement, which the verifier asserts. Each contract section carries a transcription_status of literal or inferred. docs/official_sources.json records every page URL, the operation it documents and the date fetched.
inferred_sections: authentication header value format (the security schema page states apiKey/Authorization/header but no Bearer prefix)
the placement precheck rule, assembled from the documented Region and FabricVsphereDatastore fields plus the absence of any documented 404 on createVsphereStorageProfile
